questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was interested in Armenia's long history as a cultural meeting pot, but the most compelling aspect was definitely its strong Persian department at Yerevan State University, and the country's closeness to Iran.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a very good experience, despite some trouble at the start because of a mismatch between how the courses were described and how I came to experience them. However, after the first month, I loved it there.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult. The country was a new participant to Erasmus+ and the information was disorganized and scattered all about, despite the best and most helpful efforts of my professors and the university officials.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much, unfortunately. My own home university of Copenhagen was not very helpful at all, but after I got to know them, the International Cooperation Office at Yerevan State University really did their best to be helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think that as a new student, they were not very helpful, but after I learned about the Foreign Students Office and International Students Office, and got used to asking my professors, I felt really well taken care of.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was not very hard at all! On a Danish budget, Armenian housing is very cheap, but I definitely recommend getting
list.am
, which makes it much easier to look for. I personally really recommend Kenut Hostel on 1915 Defence of Van Street near Charents Street, for anyone studying at the State University. It's really close, and the owner is super nice. In addition, there's a cheap cafeteria and multiple grocery stores nearby.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be a bit scary at first. The city doesn't seem safe at night, and parts of Yerevan can look really worn down. Don't be too scared! It's super safe. However, you should definitely prepare for the winter and bring a blanket or something, because not everywhere is properly isolated, and make sure you get everything in writing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Honestly, I didn't really experience it, so I can't comment on this. Some of my fellow students had some pretty bad experiences with it, though, and said there was a curfew, which was very off-putting to him.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Somewhat confusing, honestly. It is a mess of a back and forth between the International Cooperation Office, your home university, and searching through course lists that you aren't sure you can trust. Everyone is very nice, though, and really patient with the whole process and willing to do their best to help you. Professor Lia Evoyan at YSU is really a godsend!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First off, I contacted Professor Lia Evoyan at the International Cooperation Office and requested a course list. Then I applied for courses through pre-approval at Copenhagen University, and once I had the pre-approval I sent her my Curriculum Vitae, an Online Learning Agreement, a picture of my passport, a written application with my motivations and my academic transcript and waited until I received a confirmation. To select my courses, I messaged the individual professors listed under those courses in the Foreign Students section of the YSU webpage.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Mainly asking questions of the professors at the host university and the International Cooperation Office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk and question your professors at YSU as much as possible! Be polite, but they're all really nice and patient about helping you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very satisfied! The academic level was challenging and rewarding.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I felt the courses to be adequate to my academic level, though I should add that the courses I took with professor Liana Petrosyan were, initially, quite below my level, and it was only after we had gotten a good sense of each other that they reached a good level. This was not a flaw with her as a professor, though, just a lack of familiarity.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think that it was broadly quite similar, though it is difficult to evaluate given most of them were taught one-on-one.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Persian Language, Caucasian (Tati) Persian, Modern Iranian History, Iranian Culture, Iranian Media Domain, Iranian Literature, IRI State Order and Management Systems

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are linguistically inclined like me, do not miss out on taking a class with Professor Artyom Tonoyan. He is great, so passionate, fantastic to talk to, academically very skilled and great at challenging you. All around some of the best classes I've had. I also recommend taking classes with Professor Noonik Darbinian. She is both academically very good and also among the kindest souls I have ever met. Taking a class with her is a delight.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None that I remember.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was really cheap! Buying clothes was about the same, however.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Yerevan really is a beautiful city, and there's lots of sports opportunities, but sadly the local ballet teachers did not respond to me.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I am not aware of any dedicated specifically to students of YSU. However, there is a local Erasmus+ group for foreign students which does regular activities like going to Gyumri or seeing Khor Virap or similar.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I definitely recommend watching a performance by the National Armenian Ballet!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The National Ballet, Khor Virap, Gyumri, Lake Van... there are so many places to see in Armenia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was a little difficult, because most Armenians do not speak English.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I definitely recommend learning some basic Russian phrases, and how to read Cyrillic. This will make it a lot easier.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Armenians are very conservative, so as an LGBT+ student, this was a little scary sometimes.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Armenians are SO RELAXED. Coming from Denmark, which is very formalistic and bureaucratic, where everything has to be scheduled and done by email, it was so refreshing you could just walk up and talk to someone in the flesh, as well as how loose and informal people would be with things.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You are coming from a country that is very strictly rules-based, formalistic, scheduling-based etc. Armenia is not like that. If you are attached to those things, like having clear schedules and a clear framework, then you need to keep that in mind.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can use Yandex for basically everything. It's crazy.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Definitely, the most rewarding part was getting to know my professors and the slow feeling of getting better and improving, where I had originally feared I would not be able to.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Working on my bachelor's thesis at the same time as I was there.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
